conventions.convention: The line-search constants satisfy 0<c1<c2<1/2. Descent means gᵀp<0. Wolfe curvature is φ′(t)≥c2φ′(0); strong curvature is |φ′(t)|≤c2|φ′(0)|. The angle is measured from −g, with cosine −gᵀp/(||g||₂||p||₂).

Expansion starts at t=1 and doubles; zoom preserves its ordered endpoints, including reversed order. E and Z are finite trial budgets and may be zero. Domain checks precede trial evaluation; exhaustion and domain exit are failures even when a strong Wolfe interval exists.

Zoutendijk uses one L>0 valid on a set containing every accepted-step segment, a lower bound on the initial sublevel set, and an infinite sequence of nonzero descent directions with successful Wolfe updates.

The Newton–Krylov outer index runs from 0 through N, with stopping before a solve at k=N. There are at most J+1 linear attempts per update, beginning unshifted. Candidate residuals are recomputed for the actual shifted system, and acceptance requires the strict angle safeguard; otherwise p=−g is tried.

Local errors use ||v||*=||J*v||₂ and relative residuals measured in the Euclidean norm. In dimension zero the unique linear map has operator norm zero and the proof handles the singleton space separately.
The local rate theorem concerns unshifted full steps with forcing factors bounded by a fixed barη<1; it makes no assertion that globalization eventually selects that branch.
The scalar example realizes each finite prefix using a horizon-dependent inner budget M_N. Its infinite recurrence is not asserted to run with one fixed finite inner budget.

load_bearing.statement: For a C1 objective on an open domain and a strict descent direction, a positive feasible Wolfe step satisfies Armijo decrease and φ′(t)≥c2φ′(0); a strong Wolfe step satisfies Armijo decrease and |φ′(t)|≤c2|φ′(0)|, with 0<c1<c2<1/2. Every strong Wolfe step is a Wolfe step.

For a C1 square map F with F(x*)=0, invertible J*=DF(x*), and Lipschitz Jacobian on a closed positive-radius ball contained in its open domain, fix barη∈[0,1). There are r0>0, C_F>0 and C≥0 such that, when ||x−x*||₂≤r0 and J(x)p+F(x)=r with ||r||₂≤η||F(x)||₂ and 0≤η≤barη, J(x) is invertible, ||F(x)||₂≤C_F||x−x*||*, and ||x+p−x*||*≤(η+C||x−x*||*)||x−x*||*.

Let f be C1 on an open domain, bounded below on its initial sublevel set. Suppose one L>0 bounds gradient differences on a set containing every accepted-step segment. For an infinite feasible sequence x_{k+1}=x_k+t_kp_k with nonzero strict descent directions and positive Wolfe steps, the series Σ cos²θ_k ||∇f(x_k)||₂² is finite.

For a C1 objective, a nonzero strict descent direction p at x, and a positive feasible Wolfe step t whose segment lies in a set where the gradient is L-Lipschitz with L>0, t≥((1−c2)/L) cosθ ||∇f(x)||₂/||p||₂.

Under the search inputs, terminating real-valued in-domain evaluations and exact prescribed comparisons, bracketing and zoom terminate with a specified step or failure. There are at most E expansion trials and one zoom call with at most Z trials, excluding initial-point data. Every returned step is positive, feasible and strong Wolfe; these bounds imply neither an arithmetic-work bound nor successful discovery of an existing step.

For a C1 square root map with invertible root Jacobian and Lipschitz Jacobian on a closed positive-radius ball, an unshifted full-step residual recurrence with 0≤η_k≤barη<1 has a sufficiently small invariant neighborhood and a geometric error bound in ||v||*=||J*v||₂. If η_k→0 convergence is superlinear unless an exact root is reached; if η_k≤C_η||F(x_k)||₂ it is quadratic. No eventual selection by a safeguarded line-search algorithm is asserted.

For a C1 objective on an open domain containing the entire ray x+tp for t≥0, if φ′(0)<0 and φ is bounded below on that ray, then for 0<c1<c2<1/2 the positive strong Wolfe steps contain a nonempty open interval.
